text:
It's serviceable but generic. "For those who don't know me" and "I have the receipts" are both stock toast phrasing, and "trust me" is filler. The line also promises embarrassing material, so the next story has to deliver, and it has to be one the bride's grandmother can hear.

A specific detail would land harder than the claim itself: "I've known Dave for 23 years, which means I have receipts, and he knows I have them." Or name the first time you met: "I met Dave in sixth grade, when he was wearing [specific thing]. I have the photos."

If you keep your version, cut "trust me" and the line gets tighter. Also check that "known him the longest" is true; if a sibling or cousin is in the room, someone will heckle.
